# Star schema

*Generated by `scripts/describe_schema.py` from `data/warehouse.duckdb`. Do not edit by hand.*

Jan 2004 to Sep 2026. Two facts at their own grains share the airline and month dimensions.
Keys are readable and stable across rebuilds: `yyyymm` for months, IATA codes for ports and
routes, and a slug of the name for airlines.

## Tables

| Table | Type | Grain (one row per…) | Rows | Keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fct_route_month` | fact | airline × directional route × month | 87,176 | month_key, airline_key, route_key, departing_port_key, arriving_port_key |
| `fct_network_month` | fact | airline × month (whole network) | 1,918 | month_key, airline_key |
| `dim_airline` | dimension | airline (cleaned name) | 17 | airline_key |
| `dim_route` | dimension | directional route | 162 | route_key |
| `dim_port` | dimension | port, role-played as departing and arriving | 45 | port_key |
| `dim_month` | dimension | calendar month | 273 | month_key |
| `audit_national_total` | audit | month | 273 | month_key |

## Reconciliation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `fct_route_month` holds every airline-on-route row | 8,681,901 flights scheduled = 8,681,901 in staging |
| Route totals rebuilt from airline rows vs BITRE's published route totals | equal in 30,592 of 30,603 route-months |
| National total = sum of `fct_network_month` vs the published national row | 11,499,305.50 vs 11,495,634.50 flights; equal in 268 of 273 months |

Route totals are not stored: "all airlines on a route" is a `SUM` over `fct_route_month`,
so a route's total always equals its airline breakdown. The 11 route-months where
BITRE's own total disagrees are listed in [`SOURCE_PROFILE.md`](SOURCE_PROFILE.md).

## Which national total?

The warehouse's national total is the **sum of the airline network rows**, not BITRE's
published national row. BITRE defines the industry total as all services operated by the
reporting airlines, yet in 4 of the 5 months below the published row leaves out the
whole network of an airline in its first months of reporting. Summing the airline rows also
means a report's grand total always equals the sum of its airline bars.

| Month | Published national row | Warehouse (sum of airlines) | Gap | Gap % | On time, published | On time, warehouse | Gap = network of |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mar 2006 | 39,573 | 39,751 | 178 | 0.4% | 88.59% | 88.78% | no single airline |
| May 2023 | 45,681 | 46,089 | 408 | 0.9% | 74.00% | 74.02% | Skytrans (first reported May 2023) |
| Mar 2024 | 46,425 | 47,384 | 959 | 2.1% | 77.14% | 77.24% | Hinterland (first reported Mar 2024) |
| Apr 2024 | 46,511 | 47,526 | 1,015 | 2.2% | 79.17% | 79.22% | Hinterland (first reported Mar 2024) |
| May 2024 | 46,232 | 47,343 | 1,111 | 2.4% | 78.52% | 78.64% | Hinterland (first reported Mar 2024) |

The largest gap is 2.4% of flights and moves the national on-time rate
by at most 0.19 percentage points. A dbt test fails the build if a future
release opens a gap over 3% or moves the on-time rate by more than 0.5 points, so the choice
gets revisited rather than silently carried on.

## Airlines and brand history

Renamed or merged airlines keep their own rows, as BITRE reported them. `brand_family` chains
the ones that are one continuing operation, so a long trend can follow them:

| Brand family | Airlines (in order of first report) | From | To | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rex | Regional Express → Rex Airlines | Jan 2004 | Sep 2026 | Inferred from the data: last month Jun 2021, and the same 30 routes are listed for Rex Airlines from Jul 2021 |
| Virgin Australia Regional Airlines | Skywest → Virgin Australia - ATR/F100 Operations → Virgin Australia Regional Airlines | Jan 2004 | Sep 2026 | BITRE notes on using this data (otptimeserieswebnotes.txt) |

Skytrans (to Jun 2025) and Skytrans Australia (from Jan 2026) are **not** chained: there is a
six-month gap between them and no published source links them.
